rationale: Direct manager, company, government and SEC evidence supports keeping Valley of Fire Solar, LLC as a distinct manager-level solar-and-storage portfolio holdco. Primergy is the operator and Gemini/Noble Solar are subordinate projects. The 2024 continuation vehicle is the current Quinbrook sponsor vehicle, while APG owns 49% of Gemini only. Application remains blocked because the complete Valley of Fire Solar, LLC cap table is not public and a March 2026 filing discloses an individual security holder without class or percentage.
recommendedChanges: Keep and rename the canonical company to Valley of Fire Solar, LLC with Valley of Fire, Valley of Fire Solar and VoF as aliases.
Represent Quinbrook Valley of Fire Fund / Valley of Fire Continuation Fund LP as the current Quinbrook sponsor vehicle from the April 4, 2024 close.
Retire the former LCPF ownership period at the April 4, 2024 continuation close while preserving the 2017 year with date precision as year only.
Treat Primergy Solar as operator, not the owner of Valley of Fire; keep Gemini and Noble Solar/Purple Sage as underlying projects.
Do not attribute APG's 49% Gemini interest or Blackstone/Ares continuation-fund commitments as direct Valley of Fire Solar, LLC ownership percentages.
unresolvedQuestions: The complete current Valley of Fire Solar, LLC cap table, unnamed minority holders and intermediate holding-company chain remain unresolved.
Emily Cohen's security class and ownership percentage are not publicly disclosed.
The full current project/SPV list is unresolved because Quinbrook's project count and capacity changed between the 2024 closing release and current portfolio page.
The exact 2017 acquisition date and APG legal closing day are not publicly disclosed.
fieldCorrections: Do not represent the Gemini 51%/49% split as the cap table of Valley of Fire Solar, LLC.
Do not present an exact current Valley of Fire sponsor stake or complete owner roster until the security and minority-holder evidence is resolved.
